# Vennir

> Vennir is an open-source platform (MIT License) that runs DAGs of containerized steps as Kubernetes Jobs. Each step is a product that a platform team published and reviewed, running as its own Kubernetes ServiceAccount with only its own team's secrets, and handing its outputs to the next step. Other teams order those products from a catalog in a web console, through an API, or from CI, without ever holding the credentials the products use. Current version: 0.15.0 (0.x: not production-ready yet).

Key facts:

- Runs on Kubernetes 1.30 or later with a NetworkPolicy-enforcing network plugin: kind on a laptop, GKE, EKS, AKS, or an existing cluster. Installed with the `vennir` CLI or two Helm charts (Helm 4).
- A product is a container image plus a `product.yaml` contract: actions with JSON Schema inputs and outputs, the ServiceAccount it runs as, which teams may run it, approvals, and error explanations. Products live in a team's catalog repository; CI builds, tests, scans and signs each image, then publishes one signed catalog release that every install pulls.
- Security is checked twice: by the console, and again by Kubernetes admission policies on every Job (allowed namespaces and image sources, images pinned to a digest and scanned, each product's own identity, each team's registered secrets only).
- With a signed catalog and the kernel chart's `catalogPolicy` turned on (off by default), the kernel can verify the catalog's release itself and write which images run as each product into admission policies only it may update, so even a compromised console can't run an unreviewed image as a product.
- API products: a team publishes a backend it already runs through one gateway, at `/<team>/<api>/`, which forwards only what the API's OpenAPI file describes, and only for the API's own team and whoever each install's access list grants (single sign-on groups, people, bots).
- Cloud access is by federation where possible (GKE Workload Identity, EKS Pod Identity, AKS Workload Identity, short-lived tokens trusted across clouds), not stored keys.
- Free and open source; you pay only for the cluster and the cloud resources your products create.

## Pages

- [Home](https://vennir.io/): what Vennir is, how a run works, security, ordering, installing
- [FAQ](https://vennir.io/faq): short answers to common questions
- [Product tour](https://vennir.io/product): the catalog, templates, ordering, the API gateway, Observe, the chat agent, the CLI, and what isn't done yet
- [Use cases](https://vennir.io/use-cases): the repository's samples, on Google Cloud, AWS and no cloud
- [Security model](https://vennir.io/security): what's enforced, by which layer, and what isn't yet
- [Get started](https://vennir.io/get-started): installing on kind, GKE, EKS, AKS or your own cluster, then a first catalog and run
- [Docs](https://vennir.io/docs): every guide, grouped by reader
- [Changelog](https://vennir.io/changelog): each release
- [Community](https://vennir.io/community): contributing, reporting a vulnerability, the roadmap

## Guides

Running things:

- [Onboarding: from installing Vennir to your first deploy](https://vennir.io/docs/onboarding): Who does what, then every step in order: the install, the catalog, a first team, its secrets and cloud access, and a first run.
- [Finding and running things from the catalog](https://vennir.io/docs/ordering-and-the-cart): The Catalog, readiness on this install, run forms, the cart, Compose, previews, schedules, and deleting what a run made.
- [Runs, explained](https://vennir.io/docs/runs-explained): What each state means, what a failure does to the rest, retrying, running again, cancelling, and every failure code.
- [What's a DAG, and why does everything revolve around one?](https://vennir.io/docs/what-is-a-dag): The idea from scratch, mapped onto Terraform, GitHub Actions and Airflow if you know them.
- [How a value moves from one task to the next](https://vennir.io/docs/how-data-moves): One real value followed through a real run on kind, at every stop.
- [Calling the API from a pipeline](https://vennir.io/docs/calling-the-api): Submit a DAG, wait for it, read its outputs and logs, with curl and jq.
- [Bots and automation](https://vennir.io/docs/bots-and-automation): Token bots, keyless CI bots, ordering bots with signed callbacks, schedules and notifications.
- [APIs and the gateway](https://vennir.io/docs/apis): Find another team's API, get access, call it, and what each error means.
- [Observe](https://vennir.io/docs/observe): Security checks, metrics, usage, logs and the audit log, and who sees what on each.
- [Teams and roles](https://vennir.io/docs/teams-and-roles): Members, maintainers and admins, joining a team, single sign-on groups, retiring and purging.
- [Troubleshooting](https://vennir.io/docs/troubleshooting): Organized by what you see: a run, step, image, secret or sign-in that isn't doing what you expected.

Publishing products:

- [Catalog](https://vennir.io/docs/catalog-guide): The catalog repository: layout, product.yaml, templates and DAGs, API products, testing, what CI blocks, who approves, publishing.
- [Try Vennir end to end](https://vennir.io/docs/getting-started): About an hour: a trial team from nothing to a product that reads a secret and passes its output on. No cloud, no cost.
- [Secrets, explained from scratch](https://vennir.io/docs/secrets-explained): What a secret is here, how you register one, where it lives, and how it's kept from other teams.
- [Sync secrets from GCP Secret Manager](https://vennir.io/docs/sync-secrets-gcp): About 20 minutes: your team reads secrets from your own Secret Manager by Workload Identity, no stored key.
- [Getting GitHub ready for the catalog](https://vennir.io/docs/clouds-github): What vennir catalog create needs from GitHub before it makes your catalog repository.
- [Onboarding with an AI assistant](https://vennir.io/docs/catalog-onboarding-with-ai): Adding a team or a product with Claude or another assistant, and what to check by hand.

Installing and operating:

- [Setting up Vennir](https://vennir.io/docs/setup): From an empty account to people running steps, with vennir init and vennir apply.
- [Getting Google Cloud ready](https://vennir.io/docs/clouds-gcp): What only the Google Cloud website can do, before vennir init.
- [Getting AWS ready](https://vennir.io/docs/clouds-aws): What only the AWS website can do, before vennir init.
- [Getting Azure ready](https://vennir.io/docs/clouds-azure): What only the Azure portal can do, before vennir init: the subscription, your roles, a Free Trial's limits.
- [Getting your computer ready](https://vennir.io/docs/clouds-computer): What to install first, on macOS, Linux or Windows in WSL 2, and how to check it.
- [Operations](https://vennir.io/docs/operations): kind and Helm installs, upgrades, databases, rotating secrets, backups, network policies, the chat agent, troubleshooting.
- [Security model](https://vennir.io/docs/security-model): What's enforced and by which layer, where secret values live, and what isn't enforced yet.
- [Admin settings](https://vennir.io/docs/admin-settings): Every section of the Admin page: what it does, and whether it's set in the console or by the install.
- [Where to host Vennir](https://vennir.io/docs/where-to-host): kind, GKE, EKS, AKS or a cluster of your own: what each gives you, what it costs, and what changes for your teams.
- [Deploy to Google Cloud from Vennir](https://vennir.io/docs/deploy-to-gcp): Every Google Cloud step a team takes so its products can make resources there, with each product's own identity.
- [Deploy to AWS from Vennir](https://vennir.io/docs/deploy-to-aws): Roles, Pod Identity and cross-account access, so a team's products can make resources in AWS.
- [Deploy to Azure from Vennir](https://vennir.io/docs/deploy-to-azure): A managed identity per product, trusting the cluster's own tokens from AKS or anywhere else, with only the roles it uses.
- [Creating resources in every cloud](https://vennir.io/docs/every-cloud-from-any-install): Who sets up what in Google Cloud, AWS and Azure, whichever one Vennir runs in: identities, permissions, and creating GCP projects under a folder.
- [The API gateway, start to finish](https://vennir.io/docs/api-gateway): Turning it on, publishing a backend, calling it, and putting it on the internet.
- [Addresses and firewall rules](https://vennir.io/docs/addresses-and-firewalls): Which address each part uses, finding them, identity instead of allowlists, and a fixed outbound address.

Hands-on labs:

- [Lab 1: Vennir on your laptop](https://vennir.io/docs/lab-1-laptop): Install on kind, run a DAG, publish the samples, run a template and a cart, and delete what a run made. Free, about 45 minutes.
- [Lab 2: your first product](https://vennir.io/docs/lab-2-first-product): A catalog of your own, a product from the starter, tests run as CI runs them, a secret, and errors that explain themselves. Free.
- [Lab 3: Vennir on GKE, with a catalog](https://vennir.io/docs/lab-3-gke): A released Vennir on GKE Autopilot at the smallest size, priced before it's made, and a catalog whose CI publishes with no stored key. Billed.
- [Lab 4: Google Cloud projects from Vennir](https://vennir.io/docs/lab-4-gcp-projects): Projects made under a folder of their own, a Cloud Run service with grants inherited from the folder, and deletes through Vennir. Billed.
- [Lab 5: AWS from a GKE install](https://vennir.io/docs/lab-5-aws-from-gke): An S3 bucket and an ECS Express service, each product as an IAM role of its own by web identity, no AWS cluster and no key. Billed.
- [Lab 6: Azure from a GKE install](https://vennir.io/docs/lab-6-azure-from-gke): A resource group, a Container App and PostgreSQL, each product a managed identity of its own, and a Key Vault secret synced. Billed.
- [Lab 7: APIs on every cloud, through the gateway](https://vennir.io/docs/lab-7-apis-across-clouds): The gateway on the internet, serving a backend on AWS and one on Azure behind Entra sign-in, and every way around it refused. Billed.

Contributing:

- [Architecture](https://vennir.io/docs/architecture): What Vennir is, the pieces, a DAG becoming containers, the product contract, data, and the design decisions.
- [The kernel, call by call](https://vennir.io/docs/kernel-architecture): The kernel's layer rules and a literal trace of submit, claim, dispatch, poll and finalize.
- [How Vennir works under the hood](https://vennir.io/docs/under-the-hood): Each Kubernetes, Helm and Postgres feature Vennir leans on, what it's for, and where it is in the code.
- [Where Vennir keeps its data](https://vennir.io/docs/database-schemas): Both databases, table by table, kept in step with the models by tests.
- [vennir: design](https://vennir.io/docs/cli-design): The installer CLI: its commands, init's questions, the approval screen and cost, the OpenTofu modules.
- [Repository map](https://vennir.io/docs/repository-map): Every folder and file in the repository, one line each.
- [Architecture assessment](https://vennir.io/docs/assessment): Where Vennir is going: consumers and templates, identity in two layers, one catalog pulled by many installs.
- [Contributing and AGENTS.md](https://vennir.io/docs/contributing): What a pull request needs. AGENTS.md has the current build and test commands for each project.
